Definition: of Hebrew origin (H8095); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites:--Simon. Compare G4826.
BiblicalUsage: Simon is the name of nine men in the New Testament, but one Simon towers above the rest. Simon called Peter was the fisherman Jesus saw casting a net in Galilee, who fell at His knees confessing himself a sinful man, and whom the risen Lord asked three times whether he loved Him, then told him to feed His lambs.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Simon Peter is the proof that failure is not final, because the man who denied Him was the man He trusted with His sheep.
